full.description: This image is a gross specimen photograph of a coronal section of the brain. Multiple well-circumscribed, cystic lesions with pale contents are scattered throughout the cerebral white matter and cortex. These lesions represent multiple brain abscesses, commonly associated with systemic infections or immunocompromised states. The surrounding brain parenchyma shows mild edema and tissue distortion. The ventricles are visible and slightly prominent.

blind.description: This is a gross specimen of heart tissue from the cardiovascular system. The visual findings are consistent with a recent myocardial infarction of the free wall, estimated to be approximately six days old. Such tissue changes are often observed in patients with underlying conditions such as diabetes mellitus and hypertension. The most likely diagnosis is a healing myocardial infarction.

random.description: This image shows a coronal section of a brain gross specimen. Multiple cystic, gelatinous lesions are visible within the white matter and cerebral cortex. These lesions are characteristic of cryptococcal brain infection, commonly known as 'soap bubble' lesions caused by Cryptococcus neoformans.
